title: The match ball
summary: Your first hat-trick, and the referee has the match ball under his arm, because he keeps one from every game. You want it. A season on, he's refereeing you again.

ends.title: The ball
ends.text: The referee gave you the match ball from your first hat-trick. You both signed it. He says it's the only one he's ever given away.

ends.title: His shed
ends.text: The referee kept the match ball from your first hat-trick. It's in his shed with four hundred others. He sends you a photo of it every year.

beats.title: Three

event.title: Three
event.speaker: referee
setup: Your first hat-trick. At the whistle {referee.name} has the match ball under his arm, walking off. You know referees keep balls. You didn't know he'd keep this one.

say: "Every game I've done, one ball. Four hundred and twelve. They're in my shed." He holds it tighter.

replies.label: "Can I have it? Please. First one."
"I'll swap you my shirt for it."

ask.text: He looks at it for a long time. "First one." He signs it, then holds it out for you to sign. "Only one I've ever given away. Don't tell anyone."

swap.text: "I can't take a shirt off a player." He gives you the ball anyway, and asks you to sign one for his grandson.

leave.text: He nods, pleased. "Shed number four hundred and thirteen." He takes a photo of it for you.

beats.hint: The referee has something you want

beats.title: The shed

event.title: The shed
event.speaker: referee
setup: A photo from the referee, through the club: his shed, floor to ceiling with match balls, each with a date on in marker. {if arc.path=='given'}There's a gap on the second shelf with your name on a label.{/if}

say: "Thought you'd like to see where they live."

replies.label: Ask if you can see it.
Send him a signed ball for the gap.

visit.text: His wife makes a cake. He talks for two hours about every ball. Yours is the only one with a hat-trick.

ball.text: It goes on the shelf with a label: FROM THE LAD.

ignore.text: You let it go, and get on with your day.

beats.hint: The referee has a photo of his shed

beats.title: The same ref

event.title: The same ref
event.speaker: referee
setup: A season on. {referee.short} is doing your game. In the tunnel he says, very quietly, "Shed's full. I'm on to the garage now."
{if arc.deep=='visit'}He still mentions the afternoon in his shed.{/if}

outcomes.text: "Yours is still the only one I gave away," he says. "Behave today." You don't get booked.
He shows you a photo on his phone: your ball, in the shed, on its own shelf, with a little label.

choices.label: "Can I see the shed one day?"

outcomes.text: "After you retire." He means it. He sends you a photo of shelf four hundred and thirteen every year.
"There's a gap where yours should be," he says. "I look at it every week."

beats.hint: A season on, the same referee
